misclassified_entities.reason: EXT-NODE is described as the Ethereum node providing subscription service. In the context of a node operator, this is the local node itself and is trusted for its own notifications. However, if this represents a remote node provider, it should be SEMI_TRUSTED.
misclassified_entities.recommendation: Clarify if this is local node (internal) or remote node service (external SEMI_TRUSTED)

trusted_external_entities.name: User Application
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApp or wallet subscribing to transaction inclusion events via JSON-RPC. Subscription requests and transaction parameters are untrusted; validation required for all inputs.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application submitting transactions and monitoring for inclusion. All submitted transaction data is untrusted and must be validated using standard eth_sendRawTransaction rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Another Ethereum node communicating via eth/65 protocol. Peers can be malicious; all protocol messages must be validated against size limits and format requirements before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: EIP Author/Champion
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Developer or team proposing an EIP for inclusion in network upgrades. Authors are authenticated through the EIP process but proposals must still go through review and consensus.

trusted_external_entities.name: Signature Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External source providing ECDSA signature components for recovery. Signature data is untrusted; curve point validation and cryptographic verification required before trusting recovered public key.

trusted_external_entities.name: Precompile Caller
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contract or external caller invoking P-256 signature verification precompile. All input parameters (signature, public key, message hash) are untrusted and must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter (Blob)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user/dApp submitting blob transactions via JSON-RPC. Blob transaction payloads and sidecars are untrusted; full validation of format, signature, KZG commitments, and versioned hashes required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node (Blob Announcements)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Other Ethereum node announcing blob transactions via eth/68 protocol. Transaction announcements are untrusted; full retrieval and validation required before accepting.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network gossip layer providing blob sidecars. All blob data, commitments, and proofs from network are untrusted; KZG validation required before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Smart Contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Contract calling point evaluation precompile to verify blob data. Input parameters are untrusted; precompile must validate versioned hash match and KZG proof.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Subscription parameters must be validated. Transaction data if provided follows eth_sendRawTransaction validation rules.
Transaction data must pass full validation before acceptance. Node operator can observe monitoring activity (privacy consideration).
Applications must implement correct logic to handle reorg notifications. Mechanism provides transparency but does not prevent reorg-based attacks.
EIP proposals undergo review by client teams before acceptance. Technical merit and security implications are evaluated before inclusion.
Signature components must pass curve point validation (Legendre symbol) and cryptographic recovery. Invalid signatures raise InvalidSignatureError.
Public key must be validated as a point on P-256 curve. Signature verification uses cryptographic DER encoding and prehashed SHA256.
Blob transaction must pass format validation, signature verification, minimum blob count, versioned hash prefix validation, and balance coverage check.
Announcements are untrusted; full transaction must be retrieved and validated before acceptance. Hash-only announcements prevent bandwidth amplification.
All blob data from network requires KZG verification. Versioned hash must match transaction, and KZG proof must cryptographically verify blob authenticity.

coverage_gaps.reason: Calling contract invokes precompile through internal EVM call mechanism, boundary edge is implicit through gas charging and input parsing
